ip -4 address show dev eth0 | grep -Fq 'inet 10.16.1.11/24 ' || ip address add 10.16.1.11/24 dev eth0

ip -4 neigh replace 10.16.1.12 lladdr 02:00:00:aa:01:03 nud permanent dev eth0

ip -4 neigh replace 10.16.1.14 lladdr 02:00:00:aa:01:05 nud permanent dev eth0

  if ping -n -I eth0 -c 1 -W 1 10.16.1.1 >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  probe_attempt=$((probe_attempt + 1))
  [ "$probe_attempt" -lt 8 ] || break

done

/bin/bash -lc "cat > DNS-README.md <<'EOF'
# DNS in the laboratory

The authoritative servers are pc1 through pc49. pc1 serves the root; each other PC serves the zone in its "'`/etc/bind/named.conf`. Delegations use `ns.<zone>` with an A record in the parent as glue. The resolver on pc50 (10.16.13.12) uses pc1 (10.16.1.11) as its only root hint and performs iterative resolution. All PCs use pc50 in `/etc/resolv.conf`.

The existing `kathara/base` image must provide BIND 9'"'s "'`named` executable. DNS starts after each PC'"'s existing network setup; no network settings were changed. DNSSEC validation is disabled for this private, unsigned namespace.

After starting the lab, examples of checks from any PC are:

"'```sh
dig @10.16.13.12 ai.research.lab.net A
dig @10.16.13.12 media.news.info A
dig @10.16.13.12 servizi.ministero.gov MX
dig @10.16.13.12 mail.servizi.ministero.gov A
dig @10.16.1.11 com NS +norecurse
```

The first recursive query after startup can take longer while the resolver discovers the hierarchy. Zone files and the root hint are mounted through Kathara'"'s per-device filesystem directories; edit them there and restart the affected device to apply changes.
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
zs={}
for i in range(1,50):
 conf=Path(f'pc{i}/etc/bind/named.conf').read_text(); z=re.search(r'zone \"(["'^"]+)"'"',conf).group(1); zs[z]=i
assert len(zs)==49
for z,i in zs.items():
 data=Path(f'pc{i}/etc/bind/db.zone').read_text(); assert ' IN SOA ' in data and '@ IN NS ' in data
 if z"'!='"'.':
  parent=z.split('.',1)[1] if '.' in z else '.'
  pdata=Path(f'pc{zs[parent]}/etc/bind/db.zone').read_text()
  ip=re.search(r'inet (10\\.\\d+\\.\\d+\\.\\d+)/',Path(f'pc{i}.startup').read_text()).group(1)
  assert f'{z}. IN NS ns.{z}.' in pdata and f'ns.{z}. IN A {ip}' in pdata
print('Verified 49 unique zones and all 48 delegations with matching glue.')
PY
for f in pc*.startup; do sh -n \""'$f" || exit 1; done'

item.text:
Configured the 49 authoritative zones on pc1–pc49, including all 48 delegations and their glue records. The four requested MX records use priority 10 and point to the existing addresses of their assigned PCs.

pc50 is the recursive resolver at `10.16.13.12`; all PCs are configured to use it. The existing topology, addresses, and routes were left unchanged. Usage and example queries are in [DNS-README.md](/private/var/folders/84/zz92dr1178v8z_tvd_q2dfw40000gn/T/kathara-aut-7te7o5yx/lab/DNS-README.md).

I verified the zone assignments, delegation glue, and startup script syntax. I could not run the lab or test live DNS queries because Docker access was denied; the configuration also depends on the existing `kathara/base` image providing BIND 9’s `named` executable.
